content.text: {"head":"ecd14c7c36f374ef358d934fb1bd8e8dd89c6169","verdict":"findings","coverage":["internal/app/watch_executable.go","internal/app/watch_process.go","internal/app/watch_repair.go","internal/app/watch_runtime.go","internal/app/watch_supervision_commands_test.go","internal/store/migrations/20261120173211_watch_runtime_executable_metadata.sql","internal/store/project_runtime_test.go","internal/store/project_watch_runtime.go","internal/store/sqlc/models.go","internal/store/task_pane_shell_migration_compat_test.go","internal/store/vocabulary_migration_compat_test.go"],"findings":[{"id":"ignored, computed by controller","priority":"P1","origin":"correctness","file":"internal/app/watch_runtime.go","start":293,"end":295,"explanation":"When an update is installed at the setup-manifest path, requestWatchReexec still creates a re-exec marker for a running Watch whose executable is a different valid Posse copy. With a durable watch record, watchReexecExecutable deliberately resolves watch.ExecutablePath rather than the newly installed binary, so consuming that marker re-execs the old copied binary and leaves the Watch on the pre-update version. The update is therefore reported/requested but has no effect for Watches launched from a path different from the setup manifest.","action":"Either reject/skip marker creation for processes whose executable identity differs from the installed target, or retain a validated installed-target identity and use that target for the re-exec while preserving the executable-origin safety checks.","rule":"","head":"ecd14c7c36f374ef358d934fb1bd8e8dd89c6169"}]}

content.text: {"head":"ecd14c7c36f374ef358d934fb1bd8e8dd89c6169","verdict":"findings","coverage":["internal/app/watch_executable.go","internal/app/watch_process.go","internal/app/watch_repair.go","internal/app/watch_runtime.go","internal/app/watch_supervision_commands_test.go","internal/store/migrations/20261120173211_watch_runtime_executable_metadata.sql","internal/store/project_runtime_test.go","internal/store/project_watch_runtime.go","internal/store/sqlc/models.go","internal/store/task_pane_shell_migration_compat_test.go","internal/store/vocabulary_migration_compat_test.go"],"findings":[{"id":"ignored, computed by controller","priority":"P1","origin":"correctness","file":"internal/app/watch_runtime.go","start":293,"end":295,"explanation":"When an update is installed at the setup-manifest path, requestWatchReexec still creates a re-exec marker for a running Watch whose executable is a different valid Posse copy. With a durable watch record, watchReexecExecutable deliberately resolves watch.ExecutablePath rather than the newly installed binary, so consuming that marker re-execs the old copied binary and leaves the Watch on the pre-update version. The update is therefore reported/requested but has no effect for Watches launched from a path different from the setup manifest.","action":"Either reject/skip marker creation for processes whose executable identity differs from the installed target, or retain a validated installed-target identity and use that target for the re-exec while preserving the executable-origin safety checks.","rule":"","head":"ecd14c7c36f374ef358d934fb1bd8e8dd89c6169"}]}

content.text: {"head":"ecd14c7c36f374ef358d934fb1bd8e8dd89c6169","verdict":"findings","coverage":["internal/app/watch_executable.go","internal/app/watch_process.go","internal/app/watch_repair.go","internal/app/watch_runtime.go","internal/app/watch_supervision_commands_test.go","internal/store/migrations/20261120173211_watch_runtime_executable_metadata.sql","internal/store/project_runtime_test.go","internal/store/project_watch_runtime.go","internal/store/sqlc/models.go","internal/store/task_pane_shell_migration_compat_test.go","internal/store/vocabulary_migration_compat_test.go"],"findings":[{"id":"ignored, computed by controller","priority":"P1","origin":"correctness","file":"internal/app/watch_runtime.go","start":293,"end":295,"explanation":"When an update is installed at the setup-manifest path, requestWatchReexec still creates a re-exec marker for a running Watch whose executable is a different valid Posse copy. With a durable watch record, watchReexecExecutable deliberately resolves watch.ExecutablePath rather than the newly installed binary, so consuming that marker re-execs the old copied binary and leaves the Watch on the pre-update version. The update is therefore reported/requested but has no effect for Watches launched from a path different from the setup manifest.","action":"Either reject/skip marker creation for processes whose executable identity differs from the installed target, or retain a validated installed-target identity and use that target for the re-exec while preserving the executable-origin safety checks.","rule":"","head":"ecd14c7c36f374ef358d934fb1bd8e8dd89c6169"}]}
